resources.string:
Practise outside your actual prayer, at your own pace. This lesson walks through two rak‘ahs prayed on your own—not the additional rak‘ahs of Maghrib or a four-rak‘ah prayer.

Before an actual prayer: check its time, make wudu (or the appropriate purification), use a clean place and clothing, cover appropriately, face the qibla, and intend the prayer in your heart.

If standing is not possible, pray sitting; if sitting is not possible, pray on your side. Do not force painful movements. Ask a trusted teacher for guidance on your circumstances.
Learning preview: wording and artwork await qualified religious review. Authentic variations exist; the illustrations are aids, not a judgement on other valid ways of praying.

You have walked through both rak‘ahs. Take your time learning the words and movements; a trusted teacher can help you practise pronunciation and posture.\n\nCompleting this lesson does not record an actual prayer or mark one as prayed.
This lesson follows reports about the Prophet’s ﷺ prayer. More than one authentic wording or posture detail is reported. Read the references below; illustrations do not establish a religious ruling.
Recite the Arabic text. Transliterations and translated meanings are learning aids.
Could not open this reference. Please try again with a browser installed.
Stand facing the qibla. Raise both hands to shoulder level and say Allahu akbar. Then place your right hand over your left forearm. Begin calmly.
Remain standing, right hand over left. Recite Al-Fatihah, say Amin, then recite another passage of the Qur’an. Al-Ikhlas is provided here as one example—not a required choice. Take your time.
Raise your hands to shoulder level and say Allahu akbar as you bow. Rest your hands on your knees, with your back level and head aligned with it. Settle before reciting.
Rise from bowing while raising your hands and saying Sami‘a Allahu liman hamidah. Once upright, say Rabbana wa laka al-hamd. Pause until you are settled.
Say Allahu akbar as you lower into prostration. Place your forehead and nose, both palms, both knees, and the toes of both feet on the ground. Keep your forearms raised. Settle before reciting.

Say Allahu akbar as you rise to sit. Sit calmly with your hands on your thighs. A reported sitting posture is to sit on the left foot with the right foot upright. Ask for help adapting this if needed.
Say Allahu akbar and prostrate again. This is the second prostration of this rak‘ah. Settle fully, then recite.
Say Allahu akbar as you rise to stand. Recite Al-Fatihah again, say Amin, then another passage. The remaining movements are shown individually—there is no need to remember a repeat shortcut.
After the second prostration of rak‘ah two, say Allahu akbar and sit for the final testimony. Rest your hands on your thighs; point with the right index finger during the testimony. Remain calm.
Remain seated. Ask Allah to bless the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and his family.
Still seated, seek Allah’s protection with this supplication. You may then make other suitable supplications before ending the prayer.
While seated, turn your head to your own right and say the greeting below. Right means your right—not the right side of the screen.
Turn your head to your own left and say the greeting again. This completes the two-rak‘ah practice sequence.
Before Al-Fatihah in the first rak‘ah, one reported opening supplication is shown below. There are other authentic openings.
Glory be to my Lord, the Magnificent.
Glory be to my Lord, the Most High.
سَمِعَ اللَّهُ لِمَنْ حَمِدَهُ\nرَبَّنَا وَلَكَ الْحَمْدُ
Sami‘a Allahu liman hamidah.\nRabbana wa laka al-hamd.
Allah hears the one who praises Him.\nOur Lord, praise belongs to You.
May peace and Allah’s mercy be upon you.

اللَّهُمَّ بَاعِدْ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَ خَطَايَايَ كَمَا بَاعَدْتَ بَيْنَ الْمَشْرِقِ وَالْمَغْرِبِ، اللَّهُمَّ نَقِّنِي مِنَ الْخَطَايَا كَمَا يُنَقَّى الثَّوْبُ الْأَبْيَضُ مِنَ الدَّنَسِ، اللَّهُمَّ اغْسِلْ خَطَايَايَ بِالْمَاءِ وَالثَّلْجِ وَالْبَرَدِ

Allahumma ba‘id bayni wa bayna khatayaya kama ba‘adta bayna al-mashriqi wa al-maghrib. Allahumma naqqini mina al-khataya kama yunaqqa ath-thawbu al-abyadu mina ad-danas. Allahumma-ghsil khatayaya bil-ma’i wa ath-thalji wa al-barad.
O Allah, put distance between me and my sins as You have separated east and west. Cleanse me of sins as a white garment is cleansed of dirt. Wash away my sins with water, snow and hail.
I seek Allah’s protection from Satan, the rejected.

بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ
الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ
الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ
مَالِكِ يَوْمِ الدِّينِ
إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ
اهْدِنَا الصِّرَاطَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ
صِرَاطَ الَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ غَيْرِ الْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا الضَّالِّينَ

Bismillahi ar-Rahmani ar-Rahim.
Al-hamdu lillahi Rabbi al-‘alamin.
Ar-Rahmani ar-Rahim.
Maliki yawmi ad-din.
Iyyaka na‘budu wa iyyaka nasta‘in.
Ihdina as-sirata al-mustaqim.
Sirata alladhina an‘amta ‘alayhim, ghayri al-maghdubi ‘alayhim wa la ad-dallin.

In Allah’s name, the Most Merciful, the Giver of mercy.
All praise belongs to Allah, Lord of all worlds.
The Most Merciful, the Giver of mercy.
Master of the Day of Judgement.
You alone we worship; You alone we ask for help.
Guide us along the straight path:
the path of those You have blessed, not those who earned anger, nor those who went astray.

بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ
قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ
اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ
لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ
وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ

Bismillahi ar-Rahmani ar-Rahim.
Qul huwa Allahu ahad.
Allahu as-samad.
Lam yalid wa lam yulad.
Wa lam yakun lahu kufuwan ahad.

In Allah’s name, the Most Merciful, the Giver of mercy.
Say: He is Allah, One.
Allah, on whom all depend.
He neither begets nor was born.
And none is equal to Him.

التَّحِيَّاتُ لِلَّهِ وَالصَّلَوَاتُ وَالطَّيِّبَاتُ، السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكَ أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ وَرَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ وَبَرَكَاتُهُ، السَّلَامُ عَلَيْنَا وَعَلَى عِبَادِ اللَّهِ الصَّالِحِينَ، أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ، وَأَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدُهُ وَرَسُولُهُ

At-tahiyyatu lillahi wa as-salawatu wa at-tayyibat. As-salamu ‘alayka ayyuha an-nabiyyu wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh. As-salamu ‘alayna wa ‘ala ‘ibadillahi as-salihin. Ashhadu an la ilaha illa Allah, wa ashhadu anna Muhammadan ‘abduhu wa rasuluh.

All greetings, prayers and good things belong to Allah. Peace, Allah’s mercy and His blessings be upon you, O Prophet. Peace be upon us and Allah’s righteous servants. I testify that none is worthy of worship except Allah, and that Muhammad is His servant and messenger.

اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ كَمَا صَلَّيْتَ عَلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَعَلَى آلِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ إِنَّكَ حَمِيدٌ مَجِيدٌ، اللَّهُمَّ بَارِكْ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ كَمَا بَارَكْتَ عَلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَعَلَى آلِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ إِنَّكَ حَمِيدٌ مَجِيدٌ

Allahumma salli ‘ala Muhammadin wa ‘ala ali Muhammad, kama sallayta ‘ala Ibrahima wa ‘ala ali Ibrahim, innaka Hamidun Majid. Allahumma barik ‘ala Muhammadin wa ‘ala ali Muhammad, kama barakta ‘ala Ibrahima wa ‘ala ali Ibrahim, innaka Hamidun Majid.

O Allah, grant honour and blessings to Muhammad and his family as You did to Ibrahim and his family. You are worthy of all praise and glory. O Allah, bless Muhammad and his family as You blessed Ibrahim and his family. You are worthy of all praise and glory.
اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ عَذَابِ جَهَنَّمَ وَمِنْ عَذَابِ الْقَبْرِ وَمِنْ فِتْنَةِ الْمَحْيَا وَالْمَمَاتِ وَمِنْ شَرِّ فِتْنَةِ الْمَسِيحِ الدَّجَّالِ
Allahumma inni a‘udhu bika min ‘adhabi jahannam, wa min ‘adhabi al-qabr, wa min fitnati al-mahya wa al-mamat, wa min sharri fitnati al-masihi ad-dajjal.
O Allah, protect me from Hell’s punishment, the punishment of the grave, the trials of living and dying, and the evil trial of the false messiah.
The man is shown in a loose, opaque thobe covering his torso, shoulders and knees. A thobe and cap are illustration choices, not required uniforms for prayer.

The woman is shown in a loose, opaque prayer dress with a long khimar covering her hair, ears, neck, chest and arms. Her face and hands remain visible. Her feet are covered in these illustrations; scholars differ on the exact ruling about feet.

Both sets share the two-rak‘ah sequence and recitations. The female illustrations show a selected compact-posture variant, including a shallow bow with hands on thighs. That hand placement is an editorial illustration choice awaiting a supporting reference, not a verified instruction from the Prophet ﷺ. Other posture details follow the linked scholarly guidance. Please review this lesson with a qualified teacher.

Abu Dawud 641 supports an adult woman wearing a khimar for prayer (graded sahih by Al-Albani). The feet-covering report in Abu Dawud 640 has disputed attribution: Abu Dawud notes versions stopping at Umm Salamah, and its prophetic attribution is graded weak by Al-Albani. We do not present it as an undisputed prophetic ruling.
